_about: Little scenes on dungeon floors (scripts/Vignette.gd): what you see when you press E on them. 'kinds' are the scenes; 'lines' are what you read, any of which may be picked; a look's own lines (keyed by the look from Look.gd) come first when it has them. Dev may add lines here -- write from inside the world, never about the game.

camp.title: A cold camp
lines: Someone slept here not long ago. The ashes are cold but the ground beneath them is still dry -- they left in a hurry, or they meant to come back.
A bedroll, a ring of stones, a pot scraped clean. Whoever camped here ate the last of their food and went deeper anyway.
Three sets of footprints come into this camp. Two leave it.

fallen.title: Someone who didn't make it
lines: A cultivator, or what's left of one. Their hand is still closed around the hilt; their sword still points the way they were going.
They died sitting up, back against the stone, as if they'd only stopped to rest. Their pack is open. Whatever they were saving is gone.
No wound you can see. Their face is calm. Whatever took them here took them quietly.

shrine.title: A small shrine
lines: Somebody built this down here, stone by stone, and kept the candles lit. Some of them are still burning. Somebody still comes.
A broken statue, its face worn away by a thousand hands touching it for luck. You touch it too. It's warm.
Offerings at the foot of an old pillar: a coin, a dried flower, a child's carved bird. Prayers, left where nobody would hear them but the deep.

battle.title: Where a fight happened
lines: Scorched stone, scattered blades, a shield split down the middle. Whoever won this fight didn't stay to bury anyone.
The marks on the walls are from qi, not steel -- someone was strong enough to cut stone, and it still wasn't enough.
Arrows, broken spears, and a long dark smear where something was dragged away.

cache.title: Someone's stash
lines: Barrels and jars, tucked out of sight. Most of it has rotted. Most of it.
A smuggler's cache, by the look of it -- false bottoms in the barrels, a tally scratched into the wall. The last tally mark is unfinished.
Supplies, left by someone planning to come back down. They didn't.

smithy.title: A lost forge
lines: A forge someone built down here by hand, stone on stone, and worked for years. The bellows have rotted, but the anvil-stone still rings when you tap it.
Half-finished blades on a rack, a quench barrel gone to sludge, tally marks of every piece they made. The last mark is a sword they never finished.
A smith's corner: tongs, a cracked hammer, slag swept neatly into a pile. They kept a tidy forge right up until the end.

alchemy_lab.title: An abandoned laboratory
lines: Flasks and furnaces, a table stained every colour qi can be. One flask still glows faintly -- whatever's in it has been brewing for a very long time.
An alchemist's bench, the notes on it written in a hand that got shakier page by page. The last page says only: 'too much fire. always too much fire.'
Somebody refined pills down here, far from anyone who might steal the recipe. The recipe is scratched into the table. Most of it.

apothecary.title: A healer's lost rooms
lines: Bundles of herbs hung to dry and never taken down, clean linen folded on a shelf, a cot. Someone tended the wounded down here.
A healer's table, scrubbed pale. Jars labelled in a careful hand: for fever, for broken bones, for grief. The last one is empty.
A field hospital, of a kind -- someone treated miners here. There are names scratched on the wall, and most of them have a mark beside them meaning 'walked out'.

jeweler.title: A jeweller's bench
lines: Tiny tools laid out in a row, a loupe of polished crystal, a dish of chips too small to sell. Someone cut stones down here, by lamplight, alone.
A cutter's bench with a stone still clamped in the vice -- half-faceted, beautiful, and cracked clean through on the last cut.
Settings without stones, stones without settings. Whoever worked here was always about to finish something.

herb_garden.title: A hidden garden
lines: Someone grew a garden here, in the dark, under a crack of light from far above. It's gone wild -- but it's still growing.
Raised beds of carried-down soil, rows still visible under the weeds. Spirit herbs grow thickest where the gardener used to kneel.
A gardener's plot, marked with little stone tags. The tags name plants you've never heard of. Some of the plants are still here.

battle: The slag here has fused around a sword. Whoever dropped it was standing where the floor melted.
fallen: A smith, apron still on, hammer still in hand. The forge they were tending has been cold a long time; they haven't.
Ribs, huge, curved over a much smaller skeleton -- someone sheltered inside the dragon's bones, and stayed.
Waterlogged robes, a court seal on a cord. A palace official, still waiting for an audience that will never come.
shrine: A shrine to the river. The water has risen over its first step, and its second, and someone has kept moving the candles up.

camp: A camp strung up off the ground in a net of vines. Smart -- the floor here moves at night.

fallen: They're overgrown. Not decayed -- overgrown, gently, by pale caps that glow a little brighter near the heart.

shrine: Someone has tuned these crystals by chipping them, one tone at a time, until the little alcove hums a single chord.

fallen: Ten thousand swords in this grave, and this one disciple died with none -- their hands are empty, reaching for the nearest.

shrine: A clay soldier kneels here, alone, facing the wall. Someone has set a bowl of rice in front of it. The rice is fresh.

cache: Grave goods, quietly stolen and quietly hidden: jade, silver, a funeral mask. The thief left a note to the dead apologising.

camp: A miners' rest: tin cups, a deck of cards, and a lump of star-iron someone was too tired to carry the last mile.

legacies._about: The masters who sit at a lost workshop on the upper floors (1-10). They pass on their craft once, ever -- but only to someone who has already started down that road (the craft at level 2 or better).

masters: Smith Dun of the Ninth Vein
smithing.words: The figure at the anvil turns its head -- slowly, the way stone turns. "You have callouses in the right places. Good. I never found anyone down here worth teaching. Take what I learned. Take my best work too. Don't let it rust."

masters: the Pill Saint of the Damp
alchemy.words: Smoke curls from the dead furnace, though nothing has burned here in years. "You smell of herbs and failure. So did I, once. Here: everything I ever got right. It's less than you'd think, and more than enough."

masters: the Physician of the Lower Wards
medicine.words: The seated figure's hands are folded as if over a patient. "You've bound a wound or two. Then you know the worst of it is the waiting. Take my hands -- they knew where to press -- and my last good salves."

masters: the Cutter of the Glittering Seam
the Jeweller Who Saw Through Stone
jewelcrafting.words: Light moves inside the figure's eyes like light inside a cut stone. "You've held a gem and wondered what's inside it. That's the whole art, child. Take my eye for it -- and the ring I never sold."

herbalism.words: Vines have grown through the figure's sleeves and out again, and it doesn't seem to mind. "You know a leaf by its smell. Good. Here -- see what they're for. And take some seed. Plant it somewhere better than this."

legacies.turned_away: The figure at the {place} doesn't stir for you. Whatever it is waiting for, you aren't it -- not yet. (It wants someone who has started down the road of {craft}: {craft} {need} or better.)
